last_assistant_message:
I've handed this off to the rigby-capability-build agent with full instructions, since capability builds (skills/workflows/agents) run through that specialist per system convention.

My recommendation on your question: split content-pipeline into two separate workflows — `content-discovery` and `content-approval` — rather than a unified workflow with trigger branching. They already run on genuinely different cadences (scheduled 6am vs on-demand hourly), have distinct gate sequences, and forcing them into one workflow with a `trigger_type` param just adds conditional logic for no real benefit. Two linear workflows matches the existing IES convention better than one branching one.

I passed that decision along in the brief so Rigby builds directly to it rather than stopping to ask. Rigby will:
- Convert both skills to full workflows with the gates you specified, preserving all existing logic verbatim (no simplification)
- Register both in the workflow manifest(s) and evolutions/.pending-changes.json
- Retire the old skill entries with a redirect note (same pattern as chase-call-prep) rather than deleting them
- Leave everything staged, uncommitted, for your review

I'll report back once Rigby finishes with a summary of what was built and anything that needs your decision.
